name: The OG Girl Dinner
description: Bread, butter, sharp cheese, grapes, and pickles. The medieval peasant plate that started it all.
ingredients: sharp cheddar or aged gouda, sliced
steps: Arrange: Lay the 2 slices of sourdough on a wooden board. Slather them thickly with the 2 tablespoons of room temperature butter so it melts into the bread. Slice the 60g of sharp cheddar or aged gouda and lay it alongside the bread. Add a small bunch of red grapes and a few cornichons or dill pickles to fill the gaps. There are no rules here, just arrange by color and texture and enjoy the contrast of creamy butter, sharp cheese, and briny pickles.
notes: The original Olivia Maher TikTok that started the whole trend. Use the best butter you can find because it matters here.

name: Whipped Feta with Hot Honey and Walnuts
description: Creamy, salty, sweet, and crunchy. Four textures in one bowl with zero cooking required.
steps: Whip: Add the 150g of crumbled feta and 2 tablespoons of cream cheese to a food processor. Blend for a full 2 minutes, scraping down the sides halfway, until the mixture is completely smooth and fluffy. If it feels too stiff, add a tiny splash of water to loosen it.

Plate: Spoon the whipped feta into a shallow bowl and use the back of a spoon to create a deep swirl in the center. Drizzle 1 tablespoon of olive oil and 1 tablespoon of hot honey directly into the swirl. Scatter a handful of roughly chopped toasted walnuts over the top so they fall into the crevices. Serve immediately with crackers or crusty bread.
notes: No food processor? Mash with a fork and beat vigorously. Less smooth but still excellent.
storage: Refrigerate whipped feta in a covered container for up to three days. Keep the walnuts and bread separate, then stir the dip smooth and add fresh hot honey and nuts just before serving.

name: Chilli Crisp Noodles with Soft-Boiled Egg
description: Six minute noodles that taste like you ordered them from a really good spot.
ingredients: dried noodles (ramen, soba, or rice noodles)
steps: Soft boil egg: Bring a small pot of water to a rolling boil. Gently lower the 1 large egg into the water and set a timer for exactly 6.5 minutes for a perfectly jammy yolk. Transfer the egg immediately to an ice water bath to stop the cooking process, then peel it under cold running water.

Cook noodles: Boil the 1 portion of dried noodles in the same pot according to the package until chewy. While they cook, whisk the 1.5 tbsp chilli crisp, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, and 1 tsp rice vinegar together in the bottom of your serving bowl.

Combine: Drain the noodles and add them directly to the sauce bowl. Toss vigorously with tongs until every strand is coated in the spicy oil. Halve the soft boiled egg and place it on top of the noodles, letting the yolk run slightly. Scatter the 2 thinly sliced spring onions over the top and eat right away while piping hot.
notes: Fly By Jing chilli crisp is worth the upgrade over Lao Gan Ma. Add peanut butter for a satay vibe.

name: Baked Feta Pasta
description: The TikTok pasta that broke the internet. Roasted tomatoes, melted feta, done.
steps: Roast: Preheat your oven to 400F/200C. Place the 200g of cherry tomatoes and 3 cloves of smashed, unpeeled garlic in the center of a baking dish. Nestle the 100g block of feta right in the middle. Pour 3 tablespoons of olive oil over the tomatoes and feta, and sprinkle with chilli flakes. Roast for 35 minutes until the tomatoes burst and release their juices, and the feta turns golden on top.
Cook pasta: While the feta roasts, boil the 100g of pasta in heavily salted water until al dente. Before draining, scoop out a full cup of the starchy pasta water and set it aside.

Combine: Remove the baking dish from the oven. Squeeze the soft roasted garlic out of its skins and mash it into the melted feta with a fork. Add the drained pasta and a splash of the reserved pasta water. Stir everything together vigorously until the cheese and tomato juices emulsify into a glossy, silky sauce. Top with a handful of torn fresh basil.
notes: Use the best quality block feta you can find. Pre crumbled will not melt the same way.
substitutions: Rigatoni, penne, fusilli, or another short pasta all work. If cherry tomatoes are unavailable, use grape tomatoes or chopped ripe plum tomatoes; if replacing feta, choose another tangy cheese that softens well rather than a hard grating cheese.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a sealed container for up to two days. Reheat gently with a splash of water until the sauce loosens, then add fresh basil after warming.

name: Cottage Cheese and Everything Bagel Plate
description: Creamy cottage cheese, juicy tomatoes, and everything bagel seasoning make a savory plate with plenty of crunch.
steps: Plate: Scoop the 1 cup of full fat cottage cheese into a wide, shallow bowl. Use the back of a spoon to create a deep divot in the center of the cheese. Pour a generous drizzle of good olive oil directly into the divot. Shower the top with 1 teaspoon of everything bagel seasoning so the seeds fall into the oil and cheese. Arrange a handful of halved cherry tomatoes around the edges and serve with crackers or cucumber slices for scooping.
notes: Add chilli crisp instead of olive oil for a spicy upgrade. Trader Joe's Everything But The Bagel seasoning is the move.

name: Tinned Sardines on Buttered Toast
description: Briny, rich, and done in two minutes. The girl dinner for people with great taste.
ingredients: flaky sea salt, black pepper, hot sauce
steps: Toast and butter: Toast the 2 slices of sourdough until they are deeply golden and crisp. While the bread is still piping hot, spread 1 tablespoon of salted butter generously over the surface so it melts deep into the crumbs.

Top: Open the tin of sardines and lay them in a single layer over the buttered toast. Squeeze the juice of half a lemon directly over the fish. Add flaky sea salt, black pepper, and your favorite hot sauce. If you are using dijon mustard and sliced cornichons, smear the mustard on the bread before adding the sardines, and place the cornichons on top for a briny crunch.
notes: Brand matters enormously. A good tin of sardines in olive oil is a completely different thing from the cheap supermarket version.

name: Burrata with Peach and Prosciutto
description: Sweet peach, salty prosciutto, creamy burrata. Summer on a plate with no cooking required.
steps: Plate: Place the 1 ball of fresh burrata in the center of a beautiful plate. Slice the 1 ripe peach and arrange the slices around the burrata. Drape the 3 slices of prosciutto di Parma over the peaches. Tuck a handful of fresh basil leaves into the gaps. Just before eating, tear the burrata open so the creamy center spills out. Finish with a drizzle of good olive oil, a swirl of balsamic glaze, and a pinch of flaky salt.
notes: Tear the burrata open at the table so the cream spills out. Only works with ripe, in season peaches.

name: Smoked Salmon Plate with Cream Cheese and Capers
description: Deli style but make it dinner. Everything a bagel would be without the bagel.
steps: Arrange: Lay the 80g of smoked salmon slices on one side of a plate. Put the 3 tablespoons of cream cheese in a small bowl on the opposite side. Scatter 1 tablespoon of capers and the very thinly sliced red onion over the salmon. Add a handful of rye crackers, a few sprigs of fresh dill, and a lemon wedge for squeezing. Build little cracker sandwiches as you eat.
notes: Let red onion soak in a splash of lemon juice for 10 minutes to mellow the bite.

name: Avocado Toast with Everything Bagel and Chilli Flakes
description: Yes it is basic. Yes it is still perfect. The seasoning and chilli flakes make it.
steps: Toast: Toast the 2 slices of thick sourdough until deeply golden and crisp.

Mash and top: Halve the 1 large ripe avocado, remove the pit, and scoop the flesh directly onto the hot toast. Use a fork to mash it roughly right on the bread. Immediately squeeze fresh lemon or lime juice over the avocado to prevent browning. Shower with 1 teaspoon of everything bagel seasoning, a pinch of chilli flakes, and a sprinkle of flaky salt.
notes: A fried or poached egg makes the toast more substantial. Pomegranate seeds add a tart pop and extra crunch.

name: Hummus Plate with Warm Pita and Toppings
description: A good hummus plate hits different when the pita is warm and the toppings are thoughtful.
steps: Warm pita: Place the 1 pita bread directly over a gas flame or in a dry pan for about 30 seconds per side until it puffs up and gets charred in spots.

Build the plate: Spoon the 1/2 cup of hummus into a bowl and use the back of a spoon to create a deep swirl in the center. Drizzle generously with olive oil and dust with 1/4 teaspoon of smoked paprika. Arrange the halved cherry tomatoes, sliced cucumber, and olives around the hummus. Tear the warm pita into wedges and serve alongside for dipping.
notes: Sabra is fine but Ithaca or Oren's Hummus will genuinely change the dish.

name: Lazy Mac and Cheese
description: Kraft in a pot, made correctly. Extra butter, black pepper, and no apologies.
ingredients: Kraft mac and cheese or Annie's
salted butter (more than the box says)
hot sauce, extra shredded cheese, breadcrumbs
steps: Cook: Boil the pasta from the 1 box of mac and cheese according to the package instructions. Drain the pasta, but leave about a tablespoon of the starchy cooking water in the pot to help the sauce bind.

Make it better: Return the pot to very low heat. Add 2 tablespoons of salted butter (more than the box recommends), the cheese powder, and just a small splash of whole milk. Stir vigorously until the butter and powder melt into a glossy sauce that coats every noodle. Finish with a very generous grinding of black pepper to cut the richness.
notes: The secret is extra butter and less milk than the box says. Top with butter toasted breadcrumbs if you want to feel fancy.

name: Grilled Cheese Dipped in Tomato Soup
description: The ultimate comfort duo. Golden buttery bread, melted cheese, silky soup for dunking.
ingredients: American cheese or sharp cheddar, sliced
splash of cream stirred into soup
steps: Heat soup: Pour the 1 can of tomato soup into a small saucepan over medium heat. Stir in a splash of cream if you want it extra rich. Keep it warm while you make the sandwich.

Grill the cheese: Spread the 2 tablespoons of softened butter evenly on the outside of both slices of bread. Place the 60g of sliced cheese between the unbuttered sides. Heat a pan over medium low heat. Cook the sandwich for 3 to 4 minutes per side, pressing down gently with a spatula, until both sides are deeply golden and the cheese is completely melted.
Dip: Cut the grilled cheese in half diagonally. Ladle the hot soup into a mug or bowl. Dunk the sandwich directly into the soup and eat immediately.
notes: Medium low heat is the key to grilled cheese. Patience gives you an even golden crust without burnt bread.

name: Charcuterie Snack Plate for One
description: All the hits of a charcuterie board scaled down to a solo dinner plate.
ingredients: aged cheddar or manchego, sliced or cubed
steps: Arrange: Fan the 30g of salami or prosciutto out on one side of a plate. Place the 30g of sliced or cubed aged cheddar on the opposite side. Fill the middle with a handful of crackers. Add a small bowl with 1 tablespoon of mustard, and scatter handfuls of grapes, olives, and cornichons in the gaps so everything is easy to reach. Leave some white space on the plate so it does not look crowded.
notes: Odd numbers look better. Three types of element minimum. Do not crowd. Leave some white space on the plate.

name: Butter Noodles with Parmesan and Black Pepper
description: Cacio e pepe's lazy cousin. Butter, parmesan, pepper, done in 10 minutes.
steps: Cook pasta: Boil the 100g of spaghetti in heavily salted water until al dente. Before draining, scoop out a large mug of the starchy pasta water and set it aside.

Butter and toss: Return the drained pasta to the pot off the heat. Add the 3 tablespoons of salted butter and a splash of the reserved pasta water. Toss vigorously with tongs until the butter emulsifies with the starch and coats every strand. Add the 40g of finely grated parmesan and more pasta water, tossing again until you have a silky sauce.
Season: Finish with 1 teaspoon of coarsely ground black pepper and top with extra parmesan.
notes: The pasta water is the secret. The starch helps the butter create a silky sauce that clings to the noodles.

name: Scrambled Eggs with Cream Cheese and Chives
description: Low and slow eggs with cream cheese folded in. The softest, richest scramble.
steps: Whisk: Crack the 3 large eggs into a bowl and beat them thoroughly with a pinch of salt until completely uniform.

Low and slow: Melt 1 tablespoon of salted butter in a small non stick pan over the absolute lowest heat. Pour in the eggs and stir constantly with a rubber spatula, scraping the bottom and sides to form soft curds. This should take 5 to 7 minutes. Do not rush it.

Finish: When the eggs are just barely set and still look slightly wet, remove the pan from the heat. Fold in 1 tablespoon of cream cheese so it melts from the residual heat. Top with a small bunch of snipped fresh chives and black pepper.
notes: Keep it low and slow and keep it moving. Taking it off the heat early is not optional.

name: Brie with Jam and Apple on a Board
description: Ripe brie, sharp jam, crisp apple slices. The girl dinner that feels like a French picnic.
ingredients: crisp apple (Granny Smith or Honeycrisp), thinly sliced
steps: Arrange: Place the 1 wedge of ripe brie on a small board. Spoon 1 tablespoon of fig or raspberry jam right alongside it. Thinly slice half of a crisp apple and fan the slices out on the board. Add a handful of water biscuits. Drizzle honey over the brie and add walnuts if you want extra crunch.
notes: Let the brie sit at room temperature for 30 minutes first. Cold brie is a tragedy.

name: Greek Salad with Chickpeas
description: The most refreshing no cook dinner. Salty, crunchy, and genuinely satisfying.
steps: Prepare: Combine the half can of drained chickpeas, chunked cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, and thinly sliced red onion in a bowl.  Drizzle with 2 tablespoons of olive oil, 1 tablespoon of red wine vinegar, and half a teaspoon of dried oregano.
Dress and finish: Season with salt and pepper and let it sit for 10 minutes so the tomatoes release their juices.  Top with 50g of crumbled feta just before eating.
notes: Let it sit for 10 minutes after dressing. The tomatoes release juice that becomes the best extra dressing.

name: Loaded Baked Potato
description: A whole meal in a potato skin. Sour cream, cheese, chives, the works.
steps: Bake: Preheat your oven to 425F/220C. Rub the 1 large russet potato with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and a generous pinch of salt. Pierce it several times with a fork. Bake directly on the oven rack for 45 to 50 minutes until the skin is crispy and the inside is soft when squeezed.

Load: Split the potato open with a knife and push the ends together to puff up the fluffy inside. Add a pat of butter, then pile on 3 tablespoons of sour cream, 40g of shredded cheddar, a small bunch of chopped chives, and black pepper.
notes: The key is rubbing with oil and salt and not wrapping in foil. Foil steams rather than bakes and ruins the skin.
substitutions: A large Yukon Gold makes a creamier baked potato, while a sweet potato gives the toppings a sweeter base. Greek yogurt can replace sour cream, and cooked black beans can stand in for bacon.

name: Fruit and Yogurt Bowl with Honey and Granola
description: Breakfast as dinner is always valid. Greek yogurt, fruit, honey, crunch.
ingredients: banana slices, nut butter, chia seeds
steps: Layer: Spoon the 1 cup of thick full fat Greek yogurt into a bowl. Top with a handful of mixed berries and a quarter cup of granola for crunch. Drizzle 1 tablespoon of honey generously over the top. Add banana slices or a spoonful of nut butter if you want to make it more filling.
notes: Full fat Greek yogurt is non negotiable. It is thick enough to hold toppings and rich enough to feel like a proper meal.

name: Soft Pretzel with Beer Cheese Dip
description: Warm soft pretzels and a quick melted cheese sauce. Salty, satisfying, no real effort.
ingredients: soft pretzels, frozen or store bought, warmed
steps: Make cheese sauce: Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in 1 teaspoon of flour to make a roux and cook for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in a quarter cup of beer or milk until smooth. Add 60g of shredded sharp cheddar and 1 teaspoon of dijon mustard, stirring continuously until the cheese is completely melted and glossy.
Serve: Warm the 2 to 3 soft pretzels according to the package instructions. Dip them straight into the pot of warm cheese sauce.
notes: A splash of hot sauce in the cheese sauce makes it noticeably better.
headnote: Warm the pretzel until its crust is crisp and the center is soft, then make the cheese sauce over moderate heat. Add the cheddar by handfuls and stop heating as soon as the sauce is smooth so it does not turn grainy.

name: Pickles and Cheese Board
description: For when the jar of pickles IS the meal. Paired with aged cheese and crackers.
steps: Plate it: Arrange a few dill pickles, 60g of sharp aged cheddar, and a handful of crackers on a plate. If using salami and mustard, add them to the mix. The joy is in the simplicity, so just lay it out and eat.
notes: Claussen dill pickles, aged white cheddar, Triscuits. That is the holy trinity.

name: Instant Ramen Upgraded
description: Upgrade instant ramen with a jammy egg, butter, sesame oil, scallions, and chilli crisp in under 10 minutes.
ingredients: frozen corn, spring onion, sesame seeds, chilli crisp
steps: Cook: Cook the 1 packet of instant ramen according to the package instructions, but use slightly less water than recommended to keep the broth concentrated and flavorful.

Upgrade: In the last 2 minutes of cooking, crack the 1 large egg directly into the bubbling broth. Remove from heat and stir in 1 tablespoon of butter, 1 teaspoon of sesame oil, and 1 teaspoon of soy sauce. Top with spring onions, sesame seeds, and chilli crisp.
notes: Add sesame oil after the pot comes off the heat so its aroma stays intact. Taste before adding soy sauce because ramen seasoning packets vary widely in saltiness.
headnote: Use slightly less water than the packet requests so the broth stays concentrated. Butter rounds out the salty seasoning, sesame oil adds aroma, and a softly cooked egg makes the bowl substantial enough for dinner.
substitutions: No egg? Add cubed tofu during the final two minutes or stir in a spoonful of peanut butter after cooking. Frozen corn, spinach, or peas can go into the pot with the noodles. Use half the seasoning packet if your toppings are already salty.
storage: Instant ramen is best eaten immediately because the noodles continue absorbing broth. If necessary, refrigerate the broth and noodles separately for one day, then reheat the broth and add the noodles only long enough to warm through.

name: Caprese with Good Olive Oil
description: Three ingredients, zero cooking. Entirely dependent on quality. Get good tomatoes.
ingredients: ripe heirloom or vine tomatoes, sliced
flaky sea salt and black pepper
steps: Slice and alternate: Slice the 2 large ripe tomatoes and 125g of fresh mozzarella into thick rounds. Alternate them on a plate, tucking fresh basil leaves between them.
Dress: Drizzle generously with 2 tablespoons of excellent olive oil. Season aggressively with flaky sea salt and black pepper. Add a balsamic reduction if you like.
notes: This is either transcendent or boring depending entirely on ingredient quality. Buy the best tomatoes you can find.

name: Stovetop Popcorn Dinner
description: A bit unhinged but completely valid. Stovetop popcorn with real butter and fancy seasoning.
ingredients: nutritional yeast, parmesan, tajin, everything bagel, or chilli lime seasoning
steps: Pop: Heat 2 tablespoons of neutral oil in a large pot over medium high. Add 3 test kernels and cover. When they pop, add the rest of the kernels, cover, and shake the pot every 30 seconds until popping slows.
Season: Transfer to a bowl, immediately toss with 2 tablespoons of melted butter, flaky salt, and your seasoning of choice so it sticks to the hot kernels.
notes: Stovetop popcorn stays crisp and lets you control the butter and salt. Savory nutritional yeast is especially good with chilli powder.
headnote: Use a pot wide enough for the kernels to sit mostly in one layer and shake it occasionally as they pop. Pour the butter in a thin stream while tossing so the seasoning reaches the whole bowl without creating soggy patches.

name: Ricotta Toast with Honey and Pistachios
description: Crisp sourdough with whipped ricotta, honey, pistachios, flaky salt, and lemon zest, portioned for one.
ingredients: thick sourdough or country bread, toasted
steps: Toast: Toast the 2 slices of thick sourdough until deeply golden.

Top: Spread a generous layer of 4 tablespoons of whole milk ricotta on each slice. Drizzle with 1 tablespoon of good honey, scatter 2 tablespoons of roughly chopped pistachios, and finish with a pinch of flaky salt. Add lemon zest or fresh thyme for extra flavor.
notes: Whole-milk ricotta gives the creamiest result. Beat it vigorously with a fork for 30 seconds, or blend it briefly, before seasoning and spreading.
headnote: Toast the bread darker than you would for breakfast so it stays crisp beneath the ricotta. Season the cheese with a pinch of salt before spreading it, then add honey sparingly enough that the pistachios still taste nutty.
substitutions: Cottage cheese blended until smooth or softened goat cheese can replace ricotta. Use almonds or walnuts instead of pistachios, and maple syrup instead of honey. Choose thick bread that can support the topping without bending.
storage: Keep seasoned ricotta covered in the refrigerator for up to two days. Store the bread and nuts separately, then toast fresh and assemble just before eating so the base remains crisp.

name: Brie and Raspberry Quesadilla
description: Sweet savory quesadilla that sounds wrong but is absolutely right.
steps: Build: Spread 1 tablespoon of raspberry jam on one half of the 1 large flour tortilla. Lay 60g of thinly sliced brie on top and fold it over.

Cook: Melt 1 teaspoon of butter in a pan over medium heat. Cook the quesadilla for 2 to 3 minutes per side, pressing down with a spatula, until golden and the brie is fully melted. Cut and eat immediately.
notes: Add a thin layer of dijon on the jam side for a more grown up sweet savory balance.
substitutions: Camembert is the closest replacement for brie. Mild goat cheese or sharp cheddar also works, but use less jam with cheddar. Apricot, fig, or cherry preserves can replace raspberry jam.

name: Mezze Plate
description: Hummus, tabbouleh, olives, pita. The Middle Eastern answer to the girl dinner snack plate.
steps: Arrange: Group the 1/3 cup of hummus, 1/3 cup of tabbouleh, mixed olives, and 50g of cubed feta in separate sections of a large plate or small board. Swirl a spoon through the hummus and drizzle it with olive oil. Serve the warmed, torn pita alongside for building bites.
notes: Store bought shortcuts are completely valid. Good supermarket hummus and tabbouleh are excellent.

name: Fried Egg on Toast with Hot Sauce
description: A perfectly fried egg with crispy lacy edges on buttered toast. Never gets old.
ingredients: flaky salt, black pepper, hot sauce (Crystal or Cholula)
steps: Fry the eggs: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a small pan over medium high heat until foamy and just starting to brown. Crack the 2 large eggs into the pan and season immediately. Let the whites set and the edges go lacy and crispy while the yolk stays runny, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Serve: Slide the eggs onto buttered sourdough and add hot sauce. Eat immediately.
notes: High heat and enough fat is what creates the crispy, lacy white edges. Do not be shy.

name: Antipasto Plate
description: Italian store bought excellence arranged beautifully. Artichoke hearts, salami, olives, marinated things.
ingredients: roasted red peppers from a jar
steps: Arrange: Lay out the 30g of salami, marinated artichoke hearts, olives, and mozzarella balls on a plate. Add the roasted red peppers and drizzle everything lightly with olive oil. Tear off pieces of focaccia or ciabatta to eat alongside.
notes: Castelvetrano olives are buttery and mild. Perfect for those who do not love super briny olives.

name: Brown Butter Gnocchi with Sage
description: Pillowy store bought gnocchi in nutty brown butter with crispy sage. Ready in 10 minutes.
steps: Cook gnocchi: Boil the 250g of gnocchi in salted water until they float, about 2 to 3 minutes, then drain.

Brown butter: In the same pan, melt the 3 tablespoons of salted butter over medium heat. Add the 6 to 8 fresh sage leaves. Cook until the butter turns golden brown and smells nutty, about 3 to 4 minutes.
Toss: Toss the gnocchi in the brown butter to coat. Top with 30g of grated parmesan and black pepper.
notes: Watch the butter carefully once it starts foaming. It goes from golden to burnt very fast.

name: Classic Cheese Quesadilla
description: The comfort food that requires no recipe. Just cheese, a tortilla, and heat.
ingredients: Oaxacan cheese or Monterey Jack, shredded
steps: Fill: Scatter the 80g of shredded cheese over one half of the 1 large flour tortilla and fold it over.

Cook: Heat a dry pan over medium heat. Cook the quesadilla for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and the cheese is fully melted. Slice into wedges and serve with 1 tablespoon of salsa and 2 tablespoons of sour cream.
notes: The most underrated move is a light smear of refried beans before the cheese.
substitutions: Protein here is a suggestion, not a rule. Swap Oaxacan cheese or Monterey Jack freely and let the sauce and timing lead; check doneness a few minutes early either way.

name: Cucumber Cream Cheese Bites
description: Refreshing, crunchy little bites. A snack that feels like an appetizer.
ingredients: English cucumber, sliced into thick rounds
cream cheese or whipped cream cheese
smoked salmon, capers, or sliced radish on top
steps: Top: Slice the 1 large English cucumber into thick rounds. Spread a small dollop of cream cheese on each round. Dust with 1 teaspoon of everything bagel seasoning. Top with smoked salmon, capers, or sliced radish if you want to make them fancy.
notes: Make these when you want something crunchy and satisfying with zero effort.
headnote: Cut the cucumber into thick, dry rounds so they stay rigid under the topping. Season the cream cheese before spooning it on, then add capers, radish, or smoked salmon only at the end.

name: Crispy Spiced Chickpea and Feta Bowl
description: Crispy spiced chickpeas over lemony yogurt with feta and herbs. Deeply satisfying.
steps: Roast chickpeas: Toss the 1 can of dried chickpeas with 1.5 tablespoons of olive oil, 1 teaspoon of smoked paprika, 1/2 teaspoon of cumin, and salt. Spread on a baking sheet and roast at 425F/220C for 20 to 25 minutes until deeply golden and crispy.
Build bowl: Spoon 1/2 cup of Greek yogurt into a bowl, season with lemon juice and salt. Top with the roasted chickpeas, 50g of crumbled feta, and fresh herbs.
notes: Drying the chickpeas thoroughly before roasting is what makes them crispy rather than chewy.

name: Peanut Butter Sesame Noodles
description: Sesame peanut sauce over noodles. The most satisfying thing you can make in 15 minutes.
ingredients: spring onion, sesame seeds, cucumber ribbons
steps: Make sauce: Whisk the 2 tablespoons of peanut butter, 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, 1 tablespoon of rice vinegar, 1 teaspoon of sesame oil, 1 teaspoon of honey, and sriracha. Thin with warm water until it is pourable.
Cook and toss: Boil the 100g of noodles per package, drain, and toss immediately with the sauce. Top with spring onions, sesame seeds, and cucumber ribbons.
notes: Natural peanut butter works best. The sauce keeps refrigerated for a week. Make double.

name: Guacamole and Tortilla Chips
description: A single-avocado guacamole with lime, red onion, jalapeño, cilantro, and crisp tortilla chips.
steps: Mash: Halve the 1 large ripe avocado, remove the pit, and scoop the flesh into a bowl. Mash with a fork to your preferred texture.

Season: Add the juice of 1/4 lime, 2 tablespoons of finely diced red onion, 1 tablespoon of minced jalapeño, cilantro, and a generous pinch of salt. Taste and adjust, then serve immediately with tortilla chips.
notes: Add half the lime first, then taste. Too much acid can flatten the avocado flavor, while enough salt should make the lime and chile taste brighter.
headnote: A ripe avocado should yield gently at the stem end without feeling hollow or mushy. Mash it only until chunky, season before adding the onion and jalapeño, and keep the chips separate until each bite is scooped.
substitutions: Use lemon if lime is unavailable, scallion instead of red onion, or a pinch of chilli flakes instead of jalapeño. For a larger meal, add black beans, crumbled queso fresco, or a fried egg alongside the guacamole.
storage: Guacamole is best the day it is made. Press reusable wrap directly against the surface and refrigerate for up to one day; the close contact slows browning. Keep tortilla chips sealed separately.

name: Sleepy Girl Mocktail
description: Tart cherry juice and sparkling water make a bright, fizzy mocktail with an optional magnesium addition.
ingredients: sparkling water or prebiotic soda (Olipop, Poppi)
steps: Mix: Fill a glass with ice. Pour in 1/2 cup of tart cherry juice and stir in 1 scoop of magnesium powder until completely dissolved. Top with sparkling water or prebiotic soda. Garnish with a lime wedge.
notes: Magnesium is optional. If you use it, follow the serving directions on the package and stir until the powder is fully dissolved.

name: Cold Sesame Noodles
description: Room temperature noodles in a nutty, gingery sauce. Better cold than hot.
ingredients: shredded cucumber, sesame seeds, spring onion, chilli oil
steps: Cook and cool: Boil the 100g of noodles per package, then rinse under cold water until completely cool. Drain well.

Sauce and toss: Whisk the 2 tablespoons of tahini, 1 tablespoon of soy, 1 tablespoon of rice vinegar, 1 teaspoon of grated ginger, and 1 teaspoon of sesame oil. Thin with water until silky. Toss the cold noodles with the sauce. Top with shredded cucumber, spring onions, sesame seeds, and a swirl of chilli oil.
notes: The sauce should look slightly loose before it meets the noodles. Chilled noodles absorb moisture quickly, and a stiff sauce will turn pasty instead of silky.
headnote: Rinse the cooked noodles until they are genuinely cool, then drain them very well so water does not dilute the sesame sauce. Thin the sauce separately until it falls from a spoon in a ribbon before tossing.
substitutions: Chinese sesame paste gives the deepest toasted flavor, but tahini or smooth peanut butter also works. Use rice noodles for a gluten-free bowl and tamari in place of soy sauce. Shredded carrot can replace cucumber.
storage: Refrigerate dressed noodles in a sealed container for up to two days. The sauce thickens when cold, so loosen each serving with a teaspoon of water and toss again before eating.

name: Prosciutto and Melon
description: The Italian classic that needs no recipe. Sweet cantaloupe and salty prosciutto.
steps: Plate: Lay the 1/4 sliced ripe cantaloupe on a plate. Drape the 3 to 4 slices of prosciutto over each slice. Drizzle with olive oil, add black pepper and flaky salt. Add fresh mint or arugula if using.
notes: Only works with truly ripe, fragrant melon. If the melon is not sweet, this dish is pointless.

name: Spinach Artichoke Dip with Pita Chips
description: Warm, cheesy, bubbly dip made in 20 minutes. The shareable girl dinner.
ingredients: frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
marinated artichoke hearts, drained and chopped
steps: Mix: Combine the 1/2 cup of thawed and squeezed spinach, 1/2 cup of chopped artichoke hearts, 100g of cream cheese, 3 tablespoons of sour cream, 40g of grated parmesan, and 1 clove of minced garlic in an oven safe dish. Stir to combine.
Bake: Bake at 375F/190C for 20 minutes until bubbly and golden. Broil for 2 minutes for extra color.
Dip: Let the dip stand for 2 minutes, then set the hot dish on a heatproof board. Serve with pita chips or sturdy crackers while the center is still creamy and the top is browned.
notes: Squeezing every drop of water from the spinach is essential. Otherwise the dip gets watery.
substitutions: Jarred artichoke hearts in water work if marinated ones are unavailable; drain them thoroughly and add an extra teaspoon of olive oil. Kale can replace spinach, and Greek yogurt can replace sour cream.

name: Lox Plate on Cucumber
description: Smoked salmon, cream cheese, capers, and cucumber deliver all the familiar lox flavors without a bagel.
ingredients: English cucumber, sliced into thick rounds
steps: Build bites: Slice the 1 large English cucumber into thick rounds. Spread 3 tablespoons of cream cheese on each round. Top with a small piece of the 80g of lox, 1 tablespoon of capers, a paper thin slice of red onion, and a sprig of dill.
notes: These also work beautifully on endive leaves for a more elegant presentation.

name: Adult Lunchable Plate
description: Exactly what you think. Crackers, deli meat, cheese, grapes, a little candy if you want.
ingredients: baby carrots, apple slices, a few M&Ms
steps: Separate and plate: Keep everything in distinct piles on a plate. Put the handful of crackers on one side, 3 to 4 slices of deli turkey on another, and 40g of cubed cheddar in the middle. Add grapes, baby carrots, or apple slices in the gaps. No mixing required.
notes: The joy is in the separateness. You eat each thing on its own or build your own stack.

name: Garlic Parmesan Toast
description: The simplest, most satisfying thing. Crispy garlic toast with melted parmesan.
steps: Make garlic butter: Mix the 2 tablespoons of softened butter, 2 cloves of minced garlic, and 3 tablespoons of grated parmesan until combined.
Toast: Spread the mixture thickly on 2 slices of crusty bread. Broil for 3 to 4 minutes until the edges are golden and the parmesan is crispy. Add fresh parsley and chilli flakes.
notes: Broiling rather than baking gives you the best crispy outside, soft inside texture.

name: Cherry Tomato and Mozzarella Pasta
description: Fresh blistered tomato sauce with torn mozzarella that melts into hot pasta. Summer simplicity.
steps: Blister tomatoes: Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil over high heat. Add the 200g of cherry tomatoes and let them blister and burst, about 5 minutes. Add 2 cloves of sliced garlic and chilli flakes, cooking 1 minute.
Cook pasta: Boil the 100g of pasta in well salted water until al dente, saving a splash of pasta water.
Combine: Toss the pasta with the tomatoes and a splash of pasta water. Remove from heat. Add 80g of torn mozzarella and basil. The residual heat melts the cheese.
notes: Tearing the mozzarella rather than slicing gives you irregular melty pockets throughout the pasta.

name: Edamame with Garlic Butter and Chilli
description: Steamed edamame tossed with garlic butter and chilli makes a salty, hands-on snack dinner.
steps: Cook edamame: Microwave or boil the 1 cup of edamame pods until hot, then drain.
Toss: Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a pan, add 1 clove of minced garlic and a pinch of chilli flakes for 30 seconds. Toss the edamame in the garlic butter and season with flaky sea salt.
notes: Eat by popping the beans directly into your mouth from the pod. The tactile experience is part of it.
headnote: Steam the edamame only until hot and bright green, then dry the pods before tossing so the garlic butter clings. Bloom the garlic and chilli gently and pull the pan before the garlic browns.

name: Elevated Canned Tomato Soup
description: Turn one can of tomato soup into a richer bowl with cream, butter, basil oil, and crisp crackers.
ingredients: quality tomato soup or bisque (Rao's or Amy's)
basil oil or good olive oil
steps: Heat and enrich: Warm the 1 can of tomato soup in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in 2 tablespoons of heavy cream and 1 tablespoon of butter until completely melted and incorporated.
Serve: Pour into a mug or bowl, drizzle with basil oil, and add crackers or croutons with flaky salt.
notes: Taste before seasoning because canned soup brands differ in salt and sweetness. A small squeeze of lemon can sharpen a soup that tastes flat.
headnote: Warm canned tomato soup over medium-low heat so the cream stays smooth and the bottom does not scorch. Stir in the butter after the soup is hot, then finish each bowl with basil oil and something crisp.
substitutions: Half-and-half or unsweetened oat cream can replace heavy cream. Use pesto or good olive oil if basil oil is unavailable. Grilled bread, croutons, or a cheese toast can stand in for crackers.
storage: Refrigerate leftover soup in a sealed container for up to three days. Reheat over medium-low heat, stirring often, and avoid a hard boil so the dairy does not separate.

name: Tuna Salad on Crackers
description: A proper tuna salad. Mayo, celery, dijon, capers. Scooped onto crackers.
ingredients: quality tuna in olive oil (Wild Planet or Ortiz)
steps: Mix: Drain the 1 can of tuna and combine with 2 tablespoons of mayo, 1 finely diced celery stalk, 1 teaspoon of dijon, 1 tablespoon of chopped capers, and lemon juice. Season with black pepper and mix well. Taste and adjust.
Plate: Serve alongside a pile of crackers for scooping, then finish with the listed garnishes. Serve right away while the hot ingredients are hot and the crisp ingredients still have their texture.
notes: Quality tuna makes a huge difference. Ortiz in olive oil is in a completely different league from generic supermarket tuna.

name: Goat Cheese Toast with Honey and Walnuts
description: Tangy goat cheese on toasted bread with honey. Easy, satisfying, and kind of impressive.
ingredients: sliced figs or pears, fresh thyme
steps: Spread: Spread 60g of soft goat cheese generously on the 2 slices of toasted sourdough.
Top: Drizzle with 1 tablespoon of good honey, scatter 2 tablespoons of toasted walnuts, and add fresh thyme if using.
notes: Room temperature goat cheese spreads much more easily than cold. The combination of honey and goat cheese is very nearly perfect.

name: Shakshuka for One
description: Eggs poached in spiced tomato sauce. A dramatic, satisfying pan dinner.
steps: Build sauce: Saute the half diced onion in olive oil until soft, 5 minutes. Add 2 cloves of minced garlic, 1 teaspoon of cumin, 1 teaspoon of smoked paprika, and half a teaspoon of chilli flakes, cooking 1 minute. Pour in the 1 can of diced tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes until thickened. Season generously.
Add eggs: Make wells in the sauce with a spoon. Crack the 2 large eggs into the wells. Cover and cook 5 to 7 minutes until whites are set but yolks runny.
Serve: Top with feta and parsley. Eat directly from the pan with crusty bread for dipping.
notes: Serve directly from the pan. It looks dramatic and saves a dish.

name: Cacio e Pepe
description: Only three ingredients but requires technique. Cheese, pepper, and pasta water do everything.
steps: Toast pepper: Toast 1.5 teaspoons of cracked pepper in a dry pan until fragrant. Boil 100g of pasta in salted water until 2 minutes before done, saving a cup of water.

Make sauce: Transfer pasta to the pepper pan over medium heat, adding pasta water gradually. Remove from heat, add 50g of pecorino and 20g of parmesan, and toss vigorously until emulsified into a silky sauce.
notes: Taking the pan off heat before adding cheese prevents it from seizing. The pasta water emulsion is the entire technique.

name: Tinned Fish Board
description: The elevated pantry dinner. Sardines, smoked oysters, arranged on a board with all the accompaniments.
steps: Open and arrange: Open the 1 tin of sardines and 1 tin of smoked oysters and place them directly on a board. Arrange crackers, 2 tablespoons of creme fraiche, 1 tablespoon of dijon mustard, cornichons, and capers around them. Add a lemon wedge.
notes: The open tins are part of the aesthetic. Place them directly on the board. Fishwife and Ortiz are the top brands.

name: Avocado and Egg Salad Lettuce Cups
description: Creamy mashed avocado and chopped egg in crisp lettuce. Fresh, filling, no bread needed.
steps: Make filling: Combine 1 mashed ripe avocado, 2 chopped hard boiled eggs, 1 teaspoon of dijon, lemon juice, and 2 finely diced celery stalks. Season well.
Fill cups: Spoon the mixture into 4 to 6 crisp butter lettuce leaves and dust with paprika.
notes: The avocado supplies all the creaminess the filling needs. Keep the lettuce leaves cold and dry so they stay crisp.

name: Kimchi Butter Ramen
description: Shin Ramyun with kimchi, butter, and a soft egg. The Korean midnight snack elevated.
ingredients: spring onion, sesame seeds, nori strips
steps: Cook noodles: Cook the 1 packet of noodles per instructions. In the last minute, add 1/4 cup of chopped kimchi and 1 tablespoon of kimchi juice.
Finish: Stir in 1 tablespoon of butter until melted. Fry or poach the 1 large egg separately. Top the noodles with the egg, spring onions, and sesame seeds.
notes: Aged kimchi (the sour stuff in the back of the fridge) works best. Its fermented tang cuts through the richness.

name: Medjool Dates with Almond Butter and Flaky Salt
description: Nature's candy stuffed with almond butter. The sweet salty snack that feels indulgent.
ingredients: dark chocolate drizzle, toasted almonds inside
steps: Stuff: Slice the 4 to 5 Medjool dates lengthways and remove the pits. Fill each with a spoonful of 2 tablespoons of almond butter. Pinch closed slightly.
Finish: Arrange on a plate, sprinkle with flaky sea salt, and drizzle with dark chocolate if using.
notes: The viral date bark trend started here. These also freeze well for a cold caramel like snack.

name: Sheet Pan Nachos
description: Maximum chip to topping ratio achieved by spreading everything on one tray.
ingredients: sour cream, salsa, guacamole, hot sauce
steps: Layer: Spread 2 large handfuls of tortilla chips in a single layer on a baking sheet. Scatter 1/4 can of drained black beans, 2 tablespoons of pickled jalapenos, and 80g of shredded cheese over every chip.
Bake: Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 8 to 12 minutes, until the cheese is fully melted and bubbling and the exposed edges of the chips have deepened in color.
Top and eat: Add cold sour cream and salsa. Eat directly from the tray.
notes: Eat straight from the sheet pan. It keeps them crispy and saves a dish.

name: Miso Soup with Tofu and Noodles
description: Warm, savory, deeply comforting. A proper miso broth with noodles and soft tofu.
steps: Make broth: Bring 2 cups of water or dashi to a gentle simmer. Add the cubed tofu and warm for 2 minutes, then remove the pan from the heat. Mix 2 tablespoons of miso with a ladleful of hot broth in a small bowl until smooth, then stir it back into the pan with the soy sauce and sesame oil.

Add and serve: Cook 1 portion of noodles separately according to the package, drain well, and place in a bowl. Ladle over the miso broth and tofu, then finish with spring onions, nori, and sesame seeds.
notes: Miso loses aroma when boiled. Remove the pan from the heat before adding it, and taste before adding soy sauce because both ingredients contribute salt.
headnote: Cook the noodles separately so they do not cloud or over-thicken the broth. Warm the tofu gently, take the broth off the heat, and dissolve the miso in a ladleful of hot liquid before stirring it back into the pot.
substitutions: Use red or yellow miso for a stronger broth, starting with one tablespoon and adding more to taste. Firm tofu can replace silken tofu, and soba, somen, or instant ramen noodles all work. Use tamari instead of soy sauce for a gluten-free version.
storage: Store broth, noodles, and tofu separately when possible for up to two days. Reheat the broth gently without boiling, then add the noodles and tofu just long enough to warm through.

name: Hot Honey Butter Toast
description: The most minimal toast possible. Just good bread, real butter, and hot honey.
ingredients: thick white bread or brioche, toasted
hot honey (Mike's Hot Honey or homemade)
steps: Toast and butter: Toast 2 slices of bread until golden. Spread 2 tablespoons of butter generously while still hot so it melts in.
Drizzle: Drizzle 1 tablespoon of hot honey over the buttery toast and add a pinch of flaky salt.
notes: This sounds almost too simple to be a meal, but the contrast works. Use thick bread and let it get properly crisp before adding the butter.

name: Loaded Sweet Potato with Black Beans
description: Baked sweet potato with black beans, avocado, and lime crema. A whole satisfying meal.
steps: Bake potato: Rub 1 large sweet potato with oil and salt, pierce it, and bake at 425F/220C for 45 to 50 minutes until soft.
Load: Split it open, fluff the inside, and top with 1/2 can of warmed black beans, half a sliced avocado, lime seasoned sour cream, and cilantro.
notes: Season the inside of the potato with salt and a pat of butter before adding toppings.
substitutions: Protein here is a suggestion, not a rule. Swap sweet potato freely and let the sauce and timing lead; check doneness a few minutes early either way.

name: Caramelized Onion Dip with Ridged Chips
description: Caramelized onion dip made from scratch. Vastly superior to the packet kind.
steps: Caramelize onions: Cook 2 thinly sliced yellow onions in 2 tablespoons of butter with salt over low heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deep golden and jammy. Let cool.
Make dip: Mix 1/2 cup of sour cream, 2 tablespoons of cream cheese, 1 teaspoon of garlic powder, and Worcestershire. Fold in the cooled onions and season.
Serve: Serve with ridged chips. The dip is better after an hour in the fridge.
notes: You cannot rush caramelized onions. Low and slow for 30 minutes minimum.

name: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
description: Spaghetti with garlic, olive oil, chilli, and parsley. Italian simplicity at its finest.
ingredients: fresh flat leaf parsley, roughly chopped
steps: Cook pasta: Boil 100g of spaghetti in well salted water until al dente, saving a cup of water.
Toast garlic: Warm 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add 4 cloves of sliced garlic and cook slowly until golden. Add 1/2 teaspoon of chilli flakes.
Combine: Add drained pasta and a splash of pasta water. Toss vigorously until emulsified. Add a large handful of parsley and toss again.
notes: Garlic must be sliced and toasted slowly to golden. Never brown or it becomes bitter.

name: Savory Cottage Cheese Bowl
description: Cottage cheese topped with cucumber, tomatoes, everything seasoning, and chilli crisp makes a savory bowl in five minutes.
ingredients: sliced avocado, pickled jalapenos, fresh herbs
steps: Bowl it: Scoop 1 cup of cottage cheese into a wide bowl. Arrange half a diced cucumber and a handful of halved cherry tomatoes on top. Season with 2 tablespoons of everything bagel seasoning, drizzle with olive oil or chilli crisp.
notes: Good Cultures or Kalona Supernatural cottage cheese are notably better than generic brands.

name: Panzanella
description: Tuscan bread salad. Stale bread soaked in the juices of very ripe tomatoes.
ingredients: day old sourdough, torn into chunks
steps: Salt tomatoes: Season 2 chunked tomatoes generously with salt and let sit 10 minutes. They will release juices.

Soak bread: Toss 2 slices of torn sourdough, 1/4 thinly sliced red onion, 2 tablespoons of olive oil, and 1 tablespoon of red wine vinegar with the tomatoes. Let sit 5 to 10 minutes so the bread absorbs the juices.
Finish: Add a handful of fresh basil, toss, and serve at room temperature.
notes: This only works with stale bread and peak season tomatoes. Both requirements are non negotiable.

name: Matcha Latte and Banana with Peanut Butter
description: The girl dinner that is just a drink and a banana with nut butter. Deeply valid.
ingredients: peanut or almond butter for dipping
steps: Make matcha: Sift 1 teaspoon of matcha into a mug, add 2 oz of hot water, and whisk vigorously until frothy. Pour in 6 oz of warm frothed oat milk.
Add oat milk: Serve with 1 banana and 2 tablespoons of peanut butter for dipping.
notes: Ceremonial grade matcha is not a luxury. It is the only kind that tastes good when made simply.

name: White Bean Dip with Lemon and Rosemary
description: Blended white beans with olive oil and lemon. A more interesting alternative to hummus.
steps: Blend: Blend 1 can of drained beans, 3 tablespoons of olive oil, the juice and zest of 1 lemon, 1 sprig of rosemary, and 1 clove of garlic until completely smooth. Season well with salt.
Serve: Spread in a bowl, drizzle with more olive oil, and serve with crackers.
notes: This also works brilliantly spread thickly on toast and topped with roasted cherry tomatoes.
substitutions: Use 2 teaspoons of white wine vinegar if lemon is unavailable, adding it gradually to taste. Butter beans make an equally creamy dip, and thyme or sage can replace rosemary.

name: Egg Yolk Garlic Pasta
description: Garlic pasta finished with an egg yolk. A solo carbonara for when you cannot be bothered.
steps: Cook pasta and garlic: Boil 100g of pasta in salted water. Toast 3 cloves of sliced garlic in 2 tablespoons of olive oil until golden, saving pasta water.
Combine: Toss hot pasta with the oil and a splash of pasta water off heat. Let cool slightly, then add 1 egg yolk and toss rapidly to create a creamy sauce.
Finish: Add 30g of grated parmesan, toss, and season with chilli flakes and black pepper.
notes: Letting the pasta cool very slightly before adding the yolk is what prevents scrambled eggs.

name: 4th of July Burrata Plate
description: Red, white, and blue on a plate. Creamy burrata, sweet strawberries, and blueberries for a festive, no cook girl dinner.
ingredients: flaky sea salt and black pepper
steps: Arrange: Place the burrata in the center of a plate. Arrange the halved strawberries and blueberries around it in distinct sections to emphasize the red, white, and blue colors. Tuck in fresh mint or basil leaves if using.

Dress and Serve: Drizzle the burrata and fruit generously with olive oil and balsamic glaze. Season with flaky sea salt and black pepper. Serve immediately with crackers or toasted baguette for scooping.
notes: The ultimate 4th of July girl dinner. No cooking, just aesthetic snacking. Use fresh, in-season berries for the best flavor and sweetness.

name: Stracciatella with Olive Oil and Grilled Bread
description: Creamy stracciatella drizzled with olive oil and black pepper. The simplest luxury.
ingredients: flaky sea salt and cracked black pepper
chilli oil, honey, fresh herbs, or lemon zest
steps: Set up: Spoon 80g of stracciatella onto a plate. Take a moment to check the texture and seasoning before moving to the next step.
Finish: Drizzle generously with 2 tablespoons of excellent olive oil and season with flaky salt and cracked black pepper.  Serve alongside toasted sourdough for scooping.
notes: Stracciatella is the creamy filling from burrata. Many Italian delis sell it separately.

name: Frittata for One
description: Open face Italian omelette with whatever is in the fridge. Elegant and effortless.
ingredients: sliced cherry tomatoes, sauteed spinach, leftover potato, herbs, cheese
steps: Beat eggs: Whisk 3 large eggs with 2 tablespoons of milk, 30g of grated parmesan, salt, and pepper.
Cook: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in an oven safe pan, add fillings, and pour in the eggs. Cook over medium heat until edges set.
Finish under broiler: Transfer pan to broiler for 2 to 3 minutes until golden and just set. Slice and serve from the pan.
notes: Unlike an omelette, a frittata is never folded. It is finished under the broiler and sliced like a pizza.

name: Labneh with Za'atar and Olive Oil
description: Strained yogurt cheese with za'atar and olive oil. The Middle Eastern answer to cream cheese.
steps: Plate: Spread 1/2 cup of labneh in a wide bowl. Drizzle with 2 tablespoons of olive oil and dust heavily with 1 tablespoon of za'atar. Serve with warm pita, radishes, and cucumber.
notes: Za'atar is a blend of dried thyme, sesame seeds, sumac, and salt. Find it at any Middle Eastern grocery.
storage: Refrigerate the labneh mixture in a covered container for up to three days. Keep pita and vegetables separate, then add fresh olive oil and za'atar after the labneh has lost some of its refrigerator chill.

name: Pasta e Fagioli
description: Italian peasant soup. Pasta and white beans in a rich tomato rosemary broth.
ingredients: parmesan rind in pot, extra olive oil, grated parmesan
steps: Build base: Saute 2 cloves of minced garlic in 2 tablespoons of olive oil until golden. Add 1/2 can of crushed tomatoes, 1 cup of broth, 1 sprig of rosemary, and a parmesan rind. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add beans and pasta: Add half of the 1 can of beans whole and mash the rest to thicken. Add 50g of small pasta and cook until tender.
Serve: Ladle into a bowl, drizzle with oil, and add grated parmesan.
notes: Adding a parmesan rind to the pot while it simmers adds incredible depth to the broth.
substitutions: Great Northern beans, navy beans, or chickpeas can replace cannellini beans. Use vegetable broth for a vegetarian bowl, and choose any small pasta shape that fits easily on a spoon.

name: Homemade Crunchwrap
description: Flour tortilla folded around all the Taco Bell fixings. The ultimate comfort DIY.
ingredients: seasoned ground beef or black beans
tostada shell or large round tortilla chip
steps: Layer: Spread 2 tablespoons of sour cream, 1/4 cup of beef or beans, a handful of cheese, 1 tostada, a handful of lettuce, and 2 tablespoons of salsa in the center of a large tortilla.
Fold: Fold the edges up in pleats all the way around. Press flat.
Toast: Cook in a dry pan seam side down over medium heat, pressing down, until golden and sealed.
notes: The tostada in the middle is the key structural element. It gives you that crunchy layer.
substitutions: Greek yogurt or Mexican crema can replace sour cream. Use seasoned black beans instead of beef, and swap the crisp tostada for a handful of sturdy tortilla chips if needed.

name: Prosciutto and Fig Toast
description: Salty cured meat and sweet figs on ricotta toast. A two minute fancy moment.
ingredients: fresh or dried figs, halved or sliced
steps: Toast: Spread 3 tablespoons of ricotta on toasted sourdough until the surface is golden and the edges are crisp. Move it to a plate while it is still hot.
Top: Layer 2 slices of prosciutto and sliced figs.  Drizzle with honey or balsamic glaze and season with flaky salt and pepper.
notes: Fresh figs in season are extraordinary here. Out of season, good dried figs or fig jam both work.

name: Anchovy Butter Toast
description: For the umami obsessed. Anchovies mashed into butter on very good toast.
ingredients: sliced radish, fresh parsley, soft boiled egg
steps: Make anchovy butter: Mash 3 to 4 anchovy fillets and 2 tablespoons of butter with a fork until combined, adding a squeeze of lemon.
Spread: Spread generously on hot toast. Top with sliced radishes and parsley if using.
notes: Anchovies in butter lose their fishiness and become pure savory depth. Anyone who thinks they do not like anchovies usually likes this.

name: Stuffed Bell Pepper with Rice and Feta
description: Two halves of roasted bell pepper filled with herby rice and feta. Easy solo dinner.
steps: Roast pepper: Brush 1 halved bell pepper with 2 tablespoons of oil and roast at 400F/200C for 15 minutes to soften.
Make filling: Mix 1/2 cup of cooked rice, 50g of crumbled feta, a handful of tomatoes, herbs, and a drizzle of olive oil. Season well.
Fill and finish: Fill the peppers with rice mixture and bake another 15 to 20 minutes until golden.
notes: Any leftover rice works perfectly here. Great meal to make when you have rice from the night before.
substitutions: Protein here is a suggestion, not a rule. Swap bell pepper freely and let the sauce and timing lead; check doneness a few minutes early either way.

name: Carbonara for One
description: True carbonara. No cream, just eggs, guanciale, and pecorino. Perfect.
steps: Render guanciale: Cook 50g of guanciale in a cold pan over medium heat until fat renders and edges crisp. Remove from heat.
Make sauce: Whisk 1 egg, 1 yolk, 30g of pecorino, and 20g of parmesan together with generous black pepper.
Combine carefully: Add hot pasta to the guanciale pan off heat. Add egg mixture, tossing rapidly, adding pasta water gradually until silky.
notes: If the pan sizzles when the egg mixture goes in, it is too hot. Toss the pasta for 20 to 30 seconds first, then add the eggs and loosen with hot pasta water.
headnote: Carbonara succeeds in the minute after the pasta leaves the water. Let the guanciale pan cool briefly, toss off the heat, and add reserved pasta water a spoonful at a time until the egg and cheese become glossy rather than scrambled.
substitutions: Pancetta is the closest replacement for guanciale; bacon works but adds smoke. Use all Pecorino Romano for a sharper sauce or combine pecorino and parmesan for a gentler one. Spaghetti, bucatini, and rigatoni all work.
storage: Carbonara is best eaten immediately. Refrigerate leftovers for up to one day, then warm very gently with a splash of water; high heat will tighten the egg sauce and make it grainy.

name: Everything Bagel Salmon Bites
description: All the vibes of a bagel and lox without the bagel. Refreshing, salty, quick.
ingredients: English cucumber, cut into thick rounds
capers, dill, micro greens, lemon zest
steps: Top: Spread 2 tablespoons of cream cheese on thick cucumber rounds. Top with 60g of smoked salmon and dust with 1 tablespoon of everything bagel seasoning. Add capers or dill.
notes: These are also great on endive spears for a slightly more elegant bite.

name: Creamy Mushroom Toast with Thyme
description: Sauteed mushrooms in garlic and thyme, splashed with cream, on thick buttered toast.
steps: Brown the mushrooms: Heat the butter and olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms in an even layer and leave them undisturbed for 3 to 4 minutes, until deeply browned underneath. Toss and cook for 2 minutes more.

Add the aromatics: Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 30 seconds, just until fragrant. Pour in the cream and simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, until it lightly coats the mushrooms.
Season and serve: Season with salt, black pepper, and a small squeeze of lemon. Spoon the creamy mushrooms over the hot buttered sourdough and serve before the toast loses its crunch.
notes: Do not stir mushrooms immediately. Letting them brown first is what creates the deep savory flavor.

name: Crispy Fried Rice
description: Day old rice fried until crispy with soy, egg, and sesame. The solo dinner staple.
ingredients: frozen peas, chilli crisp, leftover protein
steps: Fry rice: Press 1 cup of cold rice into a hot pan with 2 tbsp oil and let it crisp without stirring. Push aside, scramble 2 eggs, and fold through.
Add eggs: Add 2 tsp soy sauce, toss, and finish with 1 tsp sesame oil and 2 sliced spring onions.
notes: Cold day old rice is non negotiable. Fresh rice is too wet and will steam instead of fry.

name: Seasonal Fruit and Cheese Plate
description: Seasonal fruit with a few good cheeses. The no effort elegant dinner.
ingredients: seasonal fruit (grapes, sliced pear, figs, or berries)
steps: Arrange: Place 1 wedge of aged cheddar and 1 wedge of brie on opposite ends of a board. Fill the gaps with seasonal fruit, nuts, and crackers. Drizzle honey over the soft cheese.
notes: Let all cheeses come to room temperature for 30 minutes before eating. Cold cheese is a waste of good cheese.

name: 10-Minute Freezer Fried Rice
description: Using entirely freezer ingredients. Frozen rice, vegetables, egg. Dinner in 10 minutes flat.
ingredients: frozen mixed vegetables (peas, carrots, corn, edamame)
steps: Fry everything: Fry 1 pouch of rice and 1/2 cup of frozen vegetables in 1 tbsp hot oil until crispy. Push aside, scramble 2 eggs, and fold through.
Season: Add 2 tsp soy sauce, toss, and finish with 1 tsp sesame oil and chilli crisp.
notes: Microwave pouches of rice work surprisingly well for fried rice because they are already slightly dried.

name: Pan Con Tomate
description: The Catalan classic. Ripe tomato rubbed directly onto garlicky toasted bread.
steps: Rub: Rub 1 halved garlic clove firmly over 2 slices of hot toast. Rub 1 halved tomato over the toast, squeezing gently to stain the bread red.
Finish: Drizzle with 2 tablespoons of olive oil and flaky salt.
notes: The tomato must be very ripe and the bread must be hot. This is one of the great simple pleasures of eating.

name: Blistered Padron Peppers
description: Fried green Spanish peppers with flaky salt. Most are mild, some are brutally hot.
steps: Blister: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil until smoking. Add 150g of peppers in a single layer and char on one side without stirring. Toss and cook until blistered.
Serve: Pile on a plate with flaky salt. Eat immediately by the stem.
notes: Russian roulette included. 1 in 10 Padron peppers is genuinely spicy. That is part of the fun.

name: Pita Pizza
description: A 10 minute pizza using pita bread as the base. Crispy, melty, endlessly customizable.
ingredients: sliced salami, fresh basil, olives, jarred peppers
olive oil and chilli flakes to finish
steps: Assemble: Spread 3 tablespoons of sauce on 1 large pita, add 60g of cheese and toppings.
Bake: Bake directly on the oven rack at 425F/220C for 8 to 10 minutes until crispy.
Finish: Drizzle with olive oil and chilli flakes. Eat immediately.
notes: Putting the pita directly on the oven rack makes the bottom incredibly crispy.
substitutions: Naan, a thick flour tortilla, or a split English muffin can replace pita; thinner bases need a shorter bake. Use pesto or crushed tomatoes instead of marinara and any good melting cheese instead of mozzarella.

name: Warm Olives with Orange and Herbs
description: Olives gently warmed in olive oil with citrus and herbs. A 5 minute pot of wonder.
steps: Warm: Combine 1 cup of olives, 3 tablespoons of olive oil, 2 strips of orange peel, 1 sprig of rosemary, 1 clove of garlic, and chilli flakes in a pan. Warm gently over low heat for 5 minutes.
Serve: Pour into a bowl with all the oil. Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the oil.
notes: The flavored oil at the bottom is the best part. Make sure you have bread for it.

name: Creamy Tuscan White Beans
description: Butter beans simmered in garlic, tomatoes, and spinach. Italian pantry perfection.
steps: Build: Saute 3 cloves of sliced garlic in 2 tablespoons of oil, add a handful of tomatoes until they burst. Add 1 can of beans and a splash of wine, simmering and mashing some beans to thicken.
Add beans: Stir in a handful of spinach until wilted. Season. Drizzle with more oil. Serve with bread and parmesan.
notes: Lightly mashing some of the beans is what makes the sauce creamy without adding any cream.
substitutions: Chickpeas or Great Northern beans can replace butter beans or cannellini. Kale works instead of spinach but needs a few extra minutes, and canned tomatoes can replace fresh cherry tomatoes.

name: Silky Egg Drop Soup
description: Better than takeout. Silky egg ribbons in a gingery, savory broth.
ingredients: spring onion, white pepper, sesame seeds
steps: Build broth: Simmer 1.5 cups of broth with 1 tsp ginger, 1 tsp soy, and 1 tsp sesame oil. Add 1 tsp cornstarch mixture to thicken.
Add eggs: Slowly pour 2 beaten eggs in a thin stream while stirring gently to form ribbons.
Serve: Top with spring onions, white pepper, and sesame seeds.
notes: Pour the eggs in very slowly and stir very gently. Fast movement creates bits rather than ribbons.
substitutions: Low-sodium chicken stock or vegetable broth both work. Use tamari instead of soy sauce for a gluten-free bowl, and arrowroot starch can replace cornstarch in the same amount.

name: Roasted Tomato and Burrata Toast
description: Slow roasted sweet tomatoes with creamy burrata on grilled bread. The best toast.
ingredients: flaky salt, black pepper, balsamic glaze
steps: Roast tomatoes: Toss 200g of tomatoes with 3 tablespoons of oil, 1 clove of minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Roast at 400F/200C for 25 minutes until jammy.
Assemble: Top 2 slices of grilled bread with 1 torn ball of burrata. Spoon warm roasted tomatoes and all their juices over the top. Add basil, balsamic, and salt.
notes: The tomato juices and olive oil are the sauce. Make sure you get all of it out of the roasting pan.

name: Spicy Tuna Crispy Rice
description: Sushi grade tuna, sesame spiced and piled onto shatteringly crispy pan fried rice cakes.
ingredients: spring onion, sesame seeds, avocado, jalapeno
steps: Season tuna: Mix 150g of diced tuna with 1 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp sriracha mayo, and 1 tsp sesame oil. Toss gently and refrigerate.
Form rice cakes: Press 1 cup of cold rice flat and cut into rectangles with a wet knife.
Fry: Fry rice cakes in oil until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towel.
Top: Spoon tuna onto each rice cake. Garnish with spring onion, sesame, avocado, and jalapeno.
notes: The rice must be cold and slightly dried. Day old fridge rice works best.

name: Takis with Chamoy and Lime
description: Takis with fresh lime, chamoy, Tajin, cucumber, and mango for a spicy, sour five-minute snack plate.
ingredients: Takis Fuego or Flamin Hot Cheetos
steps: Plate: Pour 1 bag of chips into a wide bowl. Drizzle with half the chamoy and lime, toss gently, then repeat only if needed. Dust with Tajin and serve immediately with cucumber, mango, or jicama on the side.
notes: Start with half the chamoy and lime, toss, then taste. Takis are already salty and acidic, so a lighter hand keeps the chile and corn flavors recognizable.
headnote: Add lime and chamoy in two light passes, tossing between each, so the seasoning coats the Takis without pooling at the bottom. Serve cucumber, mango, or jicama alongside for a cool, crisp contrast.
substitutions: Flamin Hot Cheetos or sturdy tortilla chips can replace Takis. Use Valentina or another tangy hot sauce if chamoy is unavailable, and add extra mango or cucumber when you want less heat.
storage: Dress only the amount you plan to eat because lime and chamoy soften the chips quickly. Keep unopened chips at room temperature and refrigerate cut fruit separately for up to one day.

name: Overnight Oats as Dinner
description: The reverse breakfast dinner. Prepared oats with toppings eaten at any hour.
ingredients: berries, banana, granola, nut butter, coconut flakes
steps: Mix: Combine 1/2 cup of oats, 1/2 cup of milk, 1/4 cup of yogurt, 1 tbsp chia seeds, and 1 tbsp sweetener in a jar. Stir well, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
Top: When ready to eat, add toppings. Thin with a splash of milk if needed.
notes: Works as a make ahead dinner too. Prep in the afternoon and eat in the evening.

name: Creamed Spinach on Toast
description: Classic steakhouse creamed spinach reduced down to a solo toast topping. Rich and ridiculous.
steps: Wilt spinach: Wilt 200g of spinach in 2 tbsp butter with 1 clove of minced garlic. Add 3 tbsp cream, 30g parmesan, and a pinch of nutmeg until thickened.
Cream: Taste the creamed spinach and adjust the salt and pepper. Pile it over the hot buttered sourdough, then finish with a little more parmesan while the topping is still steaming.
notes: Squeeze out excess liquid from the wilted spinach before adding cream to prevent a watery sauce.

name: Mango with Tajin and Lime
description: Sweet ripe mango sliced and dusted with Tajin and lime. The refreshing solo dessert dinner.
ingredients: chamoy drizzle, chilli flakes, fresh mint
steps: Slice: Stand the mango upright and cut the flesh away from both sides of the pit. Score or peel the pieces, then cut them into slices or bite-size cubes.
Season: Arrange on a plate. Squeeze half a lime over, dust generously with 1 tsp Tajin. Drizzle with chamoy if using.
notes: The mango must be ripe. Under ripe mango with chilli is just confusing.

name: Solo Charcuterie Board with Wine
description: A proper small board built for one, with wine. This is aspirational solo dining.
steps: Build the board: Place 40g of manchego and 40g of brie at opposite corners of a board. Fold 30g of prosciutto and 30g of salami and fill gaps with olives, fruit, and 1 tbsp of nuts. Add crackers and pour a glass of wine.
Eat slowly: Let the cheese lose its refrigerator chill, then graze slowly and change the combinations as you go. Keep the crackers dry and pour the wine only when the board is ready.
notes: Never rush a board. The whole point is that you eat slowly and enjoy it.

name: Honey Garlic Butter Shrimp
description: Shrimp cooked in 5 minutes in a sticky honey garlic butter. Eat with bread or rice.
ingredients: raw shrimp or prawns, peeled and deveined
steps: Season shrimp: Pat 150g of shrimp dry and season with salt and pepper.
Cook: Add the shrimp and cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until opaque, curled, and 145°F (63°C) in the center. Pour in the honey sauce and toss for 1 minute, until it glazes the shrimp.
notes: Patting shrimp completely dry before cooking is what lets them sear rather than steam.
substitutions: Protein here is a suggestion, not a rule. Swap raw shrimp or prawns freely and let the sauce and timing lead; check doneness a few minutes early either way.

name: Smoked Oyster Toast
description: A tin of smoked oysters on buttered rye toast with hot sauce. Deeply underrated girl dinner.
ingredients: hot sauce, lemon juice, cracked pepper
steps: Toast and butter: Toast 2 slices of bread until deeply golden. Butter generously with 2 tbsp of butter.
Top: Lay 1 tin of smoked oysters on toast. Add hot sauce, a squeeze of lemon, and black pepper. Add cream cheese and shallot if using.
notes: Taste an oyster before salting. Most tins are already well seasoned, and lemon plus hot sauce usually provides all the brightness the toast needs.
headnote: Toast the bread until the center is crisp enough to support the oil from the oysters. Drain the tin lightly rather than completely, then balance its smoke and richness with lemon, hot sauce, black pepper, and sliced shallot.
substitutions: Smoked mussels or trout can replace the oysters. Use rye for a firm, savory base or sourdough for more tang. Cream cheese is optional, but if using it, spread a thin layer so it does not bury the oyster flavor.
storage: Transfer unused oysters and their oil to a covered container and refrigerate for up to two days. Toast fresh bread when serving leftovers; assembled oyster toast turns soft in storage.

name: Roasted Beet and Goat Cheese Salad
description: Earthy roasted beets, tangy goat cheese, and candied walnuts. Classic bistro salad.
ingredients: pre cooked beets (vacuum packed, not pickled), sliced
steps: Make dressing: Whisk together 1 tbsp balsamic, 2 tbsp olive oil, and 1 tsp dijon. Season.
Assemble: Dress 2 handfuls of arugula lightly and arrange with 1 pack of sliced beets, 2 tbsp of crumbled goat cheese, and a handful of candied walnuts.
notes: Pre roasted vacuum packed beets are a completely valid shortcut and nearly as good as roasting your own.

name: Tteokbokki
description: Chewy Korean rice cakes simmered in a glossy, spicy-sweet gochujang sauce, scaled for one.
ingredients: cylindrical rice cakes (tteok), fresh or frozen
fish cake slices, boiled egg, spring onion, sesame seeds
steps: Make sauce: Combine 2 tbsp gochujang, 1 tbsp soy, and 1 tbsp sugar in a pan with 1 cup of water. Stir over medium heat until combined.
Cook rice cakes: Add 200g of rice cakes and simmer 8 to 10 minutes until soft and the sauce reduces to a thick glaze.
Serve: Spoon the rice cakes and plenty of sauce into a shallow bowl. Finish with sliced spring onions and sesame seeds, then eat while the sauce is glossy and the rice cakes are soft and chewy.
notes: Soak frozen rice cakes in cold water for 20 minutes before cooking. If the sauce thickens before the centers are tender, add water two tablespoons at a time and keep simmering.
headnote: Soak refrigerated or frozen rice cakes until they bend without cracking, then simmer rather than boil aggressively. The sauce is ready when it clings to each rice cake in a glossy coat but still moves across the pan.
substitutions: Flat rice-cake slices work in place of cylinders but cook faster. Add fish cake, a halved boiled egg, or napa cabbage for a fuller bowl. There is no close substitute for gochujang; reducing the amount is better than replacing it with plain hot sauce.

name: Tahini and Honey Toast
description: Nutty tahini with honey and sesame seeds. A two ingredient toast that is weirdly addictive.
steps: Toast: Toast the bread until deeply golden, crisp at the edges, and still a little tender in the center. Move it to a plate while it is hot.
Top: Spread 2 tbsp of tahini generously while bread is hot. Drizzle 1 tbsp honey over the top. Finish with a pinch of flaky salt and sesame seeds.
notes: Good tahini is essential. It should be pourable and smell nutty. If it tastes bitter it is a bad batch.

name: Store-Bought Pork Belly Bao
description: Using supermarket char siu pork belly and frozen steamed buns. Restaurant at home.
ingredients: store bought char siu or roast pork belly, sliced
steps: Steam buns: Steam the frozen bao according to the package directions until puffed, soft, and hot through. Keep them covered off the heat so the surfaces do not dry out.
Warm pork: Warm 100g of pork belly slices in a hot pan until edges caramelize.
Build: Open bao, spread 2 tbsp hoisin inside, add pork, pickled vegetables, cilantro, and 1 tsp sriracha.
notes: Frozen bao buns are available at most Asian supermarkets and steam back to perfect in minutes.
substitutions: Small flour tortillas or lettuce cups can replace steamed bao buns. Char siu, roast pork, shredded chicken, or crisp tofu all work with hoisin and pickled vegetables.

name: Olive Oil Cake with Macerated Berries
description: A slice of Italian olive oil cake with macerated berries as dinner. Acceptable and right.
ingredients: olive oil cake, bakery or homemade
whipped cream, mascarpone, or vanilla yogurt
steps: Macerate berries: Toss 1 cup of berries with 1 tsp sugar and 1 tsp lemon juice for 10 minutes until they release their juice.
Plate: Serve 1 slice of cake alongside or topped with macerated berries and cream if using.
notes: Olive oil cake from a good Italian bakery is one of the great things. If you cannot find it, it is also very easy to make.

name: Butter Lettuce with Champagne Vinaigrette
description: Tender butter lettuce tossed at the last minute with a bright champagne vinaigrette, parmesan, and toasted nuts.
ingredients: shaved parmesan, toasted hazelnuts, sliced radish
steps: Make vinaigrette: Whisk 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tsp dijon, and 1 clove of minced garlic together. Slowly stream in 3 tbsp olive oil until emulsified. Season with salt and white pepper.
Dress and serve: Gently toss 1 head of butter lettuce leaves with just enough dressing to coat lightly. Plate immediately and add parmesan or hazelnuts.
notes: Dress the salad immediately before serving. Start with half the vinaigrette, toss gently with your hands, and add more only if the leaves still look dry.
headnote: Wash the lettuce in cold water and dry it thoroughly so the vinaigrette can cling. Tear large leaves by hand, whisk the dressing until glossy, and toss with only half at first because butter lettuce wilts quickly.
substitutions: White wine vinegar is the closest substitute for champagne vinegar; rice vinegar also works but is milder. Use toasted walnuts, hazelnuts, or almonds, and swap parmesan for crumbled goat cheese if preferred.
storage: Keep washed, thoroughly dried lettuce covered with a dry paper towel for up to two days. Refrigerate the vinaigrette separately for up to one week and whisk again before using.

name: Whipped Ricotta with Cherry Tomato Confit
description: Silky whipped ricotta topped with sweet, blistered cherry tomatoes in olive oil.
ingredients: cherry tomato confit or blistered tomatoes
flaky sea salt, black pepper, fresh basil
steps: Whip: Add 1/2 cup of ricotta and 1 tbsp olive oil to a food processor or bowl. Whip until completely smooth and fluffy, about 2 minutes.

Plate: Spoon the whipped ricotta into a shallow bowl. Top with 1/4 cup of cherry tomato confit, letting the oil pool slightly. Season with flaky salt, black pepper, and fresh basil. Serve with crackers.
notes: For quick blistered tomatoes, cook them cut-side down in olive oil over medium-high heat until they collapse at the edges, then season with salt and basil.
headnote: Drain watery ricotta before whipping so it becomes airy instead of loose. Spoon warm tomatoes and their flavored oil over the cold ricotta just before serving for a clear temperature and texture contrast.
substitutions: Roast halved cherry tomatoes at 425°F until blistered if confit is unavailable. Cottage cheese blended until smooth can replace ricotta, while toasted sourdough, pita, or sturdy crackers all work for scooping.
storage: Refrigerate whipped ricotta and tomato confit in separate covered containers for up to three days. Bring the ricotta toward room temperature and warm the tomatoes gently before assembling.

name: Smoked Trout and Apple Plate
description: Smoky trout flaked over crisp apple slices with a mustard dressing.
steps: Make dressing: Whisk together 1 tbsp dijon, 1 tsp honey, 1 tbsp olive oil, and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Plate: Arrange the apple slices on a plate. Flake the smoked trout over the apples. Drizzle with the honey mustard dressing.
notes: Smoked trout is usually found in tins near the smoked salmon. It is cheaper and very flavorful.

name: Udon Noodles in Mentsuyu with Spinach
description: Chewy udon noodles in a savory Japanese dipping broth with tender spinach.
ingredients: bonito flakes, sesame seeds, chili oil
steps: Make broth: In a small pot, combine 1/4 cup mentsuyu and 1/2 cup water. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook noodles: Boil the frozen udon according to package directions. In the last 30 seconds, drop in the handful of spinach to wilt. Drain well.
Serve: Place the hot noodles and spinach in a deep bowl. Pour the hot broth over the top. Garnish with spring onions and optional toppings.
notes: Mentsuyu is a concentrated Japanese soup base found in bottles at Asian markets. It is a pantry staple for fast meals.

name: Garlic Confit Bread
description: Crisp toast smeared with soft, sweet garlic confit and flaky salt.
steps: Toast: Toast the sourdough until deeply golden and crisp at the edges. Move it to a plate while it is hot so the garlic oil can soak into the rough surface.
Smear: While the toast is hot, drizzle with the garlic confit oil. Use a fork to smash the soft garlic confit cloves directly onto the bread. Sprinkle with flaky salt and fresh thyme.
notes: Garlic confit is made by slowly poaching peeled garlic cloves in olive oil over very low heat until golden and soft. Make a big batch and keep it in the fridge.

name: Cottage Cheese with Peaches and Hot Honey
description: Creamy cottage cheese, ripe peaches, and hot honey make a sweet, spicy bowl with plenty of contrast.
