steps: Assemble: Scoop the cottage cheese into a bowl. Arrange the sliced peaches on top. Drizzle generously with hot honey and sprinkle with flaky salt and almonds.
notes: The combination of sweet peaches, spicy honey, and creamy cheese is unexpectedly perfect.

name: Tinned Mussels in Escabeche on Crackers
description: Briny mussels in a tangy vinegar sauce piled onto crisp crackers.
ingredients: flaky sea salt, cracked black pepper
steps: Plate: Open the tin of mussels. Arrange the crackers on a plate. Place the mussels on the crackers and spoon a little of the escabeche sauce over the top. Squeeze lemon juice over and season.
notes: Escabeche is a tangy marinade of vinegar, paprika, and oil. It cuts the richness of the mussels perfectly.

name: Prosciutto Wrapped Melon with Mint
description: The classic appetizer, upgraded with fresh mint for a bright finish.
steps: Wrap: Wrap each melon wedge with a slice of prosciutto. Arrange on a plate. Tuck fresh mint leaves between the wedges. Drizzle with balsamic glaze.
notes: The mint makes this feel like a spa day rather than a lazy dinner.

name: Cream Cheese and Jelly Toast
description: Whipped cream cheese and dark fruit preserves turn crisp toast into a sweet, salty five-minute dinner.
ingredients: high quality fruit preserves (fig, raspberry, or blackberry)
steps: Toast: Toast the bread until golden.  Spread a thick layer of cream cheese on each slice.
Top: Top with a generous spoonful of preserves.  Sprinkle with flaky salt.
notes: The flaky salt cuts the sweetness and makes the fruit flavor pop.

name: Hummus and Crispy Chickpea Bowl
description: Creamy hummus topped with crunchy, spiced roasted chickpeas for textural contrast.
steps: Roast chickpeas: Toss the dried chickpeas with olive oil, cumin, paprika, and salt. Roast at 400F/200C for 20-25 minutes until crispy.
Assemble: Spoon the hummus into a bowl. Top with the warm crispy chickpeas. Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with parsley.
notes: Make sure the chickpeas are completely dry before roasting so they crisp up instead of steaming.

name: Spicy Vodka Pasta
description: The viral Gigi Hadid pasta. Creamy, spicy, and ready in 20 minutes.
steps: Make sauce: Melt butter in a pan. Add tomato paste and chilli flakes, cooking for 2 minutes. Deglaze with vodka. Stir in heavy cream and parmesan until smooth.
Cook pasta: Boil pasta in salted water until al dente. Reserve a splash of pasta water.
Combine: Toss the drained pasta in the sauce, adding pasta water to loosen if needed. Season and serve.
notes: The vodka is optional but it helps release flavors in the tomato paste that are alcohol soluble.

name: Tuna Melt in a Pita
description: A gooey tuna melt stuffed inside a pita pocket and toasted in a pan.
steps: Mix: In a bowl, mix the drained tuna with mayo, dijon, and shredded cheese.
Stuff and toast: Stuff the tuna mixture into the pita pocket. Butter the outside of the pita. Cook in a pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and the cheese is melted.
notes: Using a pita means no filling falls out when you flip it. It is the superior tuna melt vessel.
substitutions: Protein here is a suggestion, not a rule. Swap pita bread freely and let the sauce and timing lead; check doneness a few minutes early either way.

name: Tomato Soup with Grilled Cheese Croutons
description: Elevated canned tomato soup topped with cubed, crispy grilled cheese.
steps: Make grilled cheese: Butter the outside of the bread. Place cheese inside. Cook in a pan over medium heat until golden on both sides and cheese is melted. Cut into bite-sized cubes.
Heat soup: Warm the tomato soup in a saucepan. Stir in a splash of heavy cream.
Serve: Pour the soup into a bowl. Top with the grilled cheese croutons right before eating so they stay crunchy.
notes: This is the fun cousin of the classic tomato soup and grilled cheese combo.

name: Brie and Prosciutto Grilled Cheese
description: An elevated grilled cheese with melted brie and salty prosciutto.
steps: Build: Butter the outside of the bread. Place brie, prosciutto, and fig jam between the unbuttered sides.
Cook: Cook in a pan over medium-low heat for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and the brie is fully melted.
notes: The fig jam adds a sweet element that pairs perfectly with the salty prosciutto.
substitutions: Protein here is a suggestion, not a rule. Swap butter freely and let the sauce and timing lead; check doneness a few minutes early either way.

name: Soba Noodles with Sesame Soy Dressing
description: Cold buckwheat noodles in a nutty, savory dressing. Light but satisfying.
steps: Cook noodles: Boil soba noodles according to package. Drain and rinse under cold water until completely cool.
Dress: Whisk soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and sugar. Toss the cold noodles in the dressing. Top with sesame seeds and spring onions.
notes: Rinsing soba noodles thoroughly removes excess starch and gives them a perfect chewy texture.

name: Baked Eggs in Avocado
description: Eggs baked inside avocado halves make a rich breakfast-for-dinner with crisp edges and a soft center.
steps: Prep: Preheat oven to 425F/220C. Halve the avocado and remove the pit. Scoop out a little extra flesh to make the hole bigger. Place the avocado halves in a baking dish to keep them stable.
Bake: Crack an egg into each avocado hole. Season with salt, pepper, and chilli flakes. Bake for 15 minutes until the egg whites are set.
notes: Use small eggs or the whites will overflow. You can also crack the egg into a cup first and pour it in.

name: Fig and Gorgonzola Flatbread
description: Sweet figs and sharp gorgonzola melt together on a crisp flatbread finished with honey and black pepper.
steps: Assemble: Place the flatbread on a baking sheet. Top with crumbled gorgonzola and sliced figs.
Bake: Bake at 400F/200C for 8-10 minutes until the cheese is melted and the crust is crispy.
Finish: Drizzle with honey and top with a handful of fresh arugula.
notes: The peppery arugula cuts the richness of the gorgonzola perfectly.
substitutions: Use another blue cheese for the closest flavor, or goat cheese for a milder flatbread. Pear or thinly sliced apple can replace figs, and naan works in place of flatbread.

name: Cucumber and Feta Salad with Dill
description: Cool cucumber, briny feta, fresh dill, and red wine vinegar make a crisp salad that improves as it rests.
steps: Prepare: Slice the cucumber into thin rounds.  Toss with crumbled feta, red wine vinegar, olive oil, and chopped dill.
Dress and finish: Season with salt and pepper.  Let sit for 5 minutes for flavors to meld.
notes: This is even better if you let it sit in the fridge for 30 minutes. The cucumbers release their water and create a light dressing.

name: Baked Sweet Potato with Marshmallows and Pecans
description: A dessert-like dinner. A sweet potato baked until soft, then topped with marshmallows and pecans.
steps: Bake: Preheat oven to 425F/220C. Rub the sweet potato with oil and salt. Pierce with a fork. Bake for 45-50 minutes until soft.
Top: Split the potato open. Add butter, cinnamon, marshmallows, and pecans. Return to the oven for 2-3 minutes until the marshmallows are toasted.
notes: This is essentially a Thanksgiving side dish masquerading as a solo dinner.
substitutions: A small acorn squash half can replace the sweet potato, though it may need a longer roast. Walnuts work instead of pecans, and maple syrup can replace brown sugar for the finish.

name: Dark Chocolate and Almond Butter Banana Bites
description: Slices of banana topped with almond butter and dark chocolate chips.
steps: Assemble: Slice the banana into thick rounds. Spread a small dollop of almond butter on each slice. Press a dark chocolate chip into the almond butter. Sprinkle with flaky salt.
notes: The flaky salt is crucial. It makes the chocolate taste more chocolatey.

name: Cheddar and Apple Quesadilla
description: A sweet and savory quesadilla with sharp cheddar and crisp apple slices.
steps: Build: Sprinkle half the cheddar on one half of the tortilla. Top with apple slices and the rest of the cheddar. Fold over.
Cook: Melt butter in a pan. Cook the quesadilla for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and the cheese is melted. Slice and serve with honey or dijon.
notes: This sounds weird but it is essentially a grilled cheese with apple, which is a classic combo.

name: Muhammara Dip with Pita
description: A spicy, smoky roasted red pepper and walnut dip. Better than hummus.
steps: Plate: Spoon the muhammara into a shallow bowl. Drizzle with olive oil. Serve with torn warm pita. Scatter with walnuts and mint if desired.
notes: Muhammara is made with roasted red peppers, walnuts, and pomegranate molasses. It is tangy and deeply flavorful.

name: Spicy Tuna Bowl with Brown Rice
description: Sushi-grade tuna tossed with spicy mayo, soy sauce, and sesame oil makes a bold topping for warm brown rice.
steps: Season tuna: In a bowl, toss the cubed tuna with soy sauce, sriracha mayo, and sesame oil.
Assemble: Place the warm brown rice in a bowl. Top with the spicy tuna. Garnish with sesame seeds, spring onions, and avocado slices.
notes: Brown rice adds a nutty flavor and extra fiber. Make sure it is still warm when you assemble the bowl.

name: Cottage Cheese and Tuna Salad
description: Cottage cheese replaces the usual mayonnaise in this creamy tuna salad for crackers or cucumber slices.
steps: Mix: In a bowl, combine the drained tuna, cottage cheese, diced celery, dijon, and lemon juice. Mix well. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve: Spoon the tuna salad into a shallow bowl and add black pepper. Serve with crisp crackers or thick cucumber slices for scooping.
notes: The cottage cheese makes it incredibly creamy without the heaviness of mayo.

name: White Bean and Tuna Salad
description: A Mediterranean style tuna salad with white beans, red onion, and herbs.
steps: Prepare: In a bowl, combine the tuna, cannellini beans, and red onion.
Dress and finish: Dress with red wine vinegar and olive oil.  Add parsley and season generously.
notes: Let this sit for 10 minutes before eating. The beans will absorb the dressing.

name: Caprese Stuffed Avocado
description: An avocado half filled with mozzarella, tomato, basil, and balsamic makes a fresh single-serving salad.
steps: Prep avocado: Halve the avocado and remove the pit. Scoop out a little flesh to make the hole bigger.
Stuff: Toss the tomatoes, mozzarella, and basil with olive oil. Spoon the mixture into the avocado halves. Drizzle with balsamic glaze and season.
notes: Choose an avocado that gives slightly under gentle pressure so it holds the filling without feeling hard.

name: Gnocchi with Pesto and Cherry Tomatoes
description: Pillowy potato gnocchi tossed in basil pesto with burst cherry tomatoes.
steps: Cook gnocchi: Boil the gnocchi in well-salted water until they rise to the surface and stay there, about 2 to 3 minutes. Scoop them out, drain well, and keep them warm.
Blister tomatoes: In the same pot, heat olive oil over high heat. Add cherry tomatoes and cook until they burst, about 3 minutes.
Combine: Add the gnocchi back to the pot. Stir in the pesto. Top with parmesan and black pepper.
notes: Using store-bought pesto is fine, but a little fresh lemon juice brightens it up.
headnote: Cook the gnocchi until they float, then give them a minute in the pan so the edges pick up a little color. Add pesto off the heat and fold in the tomatoes last so the sauce stays green and the tomatoes keep some shape.
substitutions: Shelf-stable or refrigerated potato gnocchi both work. Sun-dried tomatoes can replace the cherry tomatoes for a more concentrated flavor, and a spoonful of ricotta can soften a very strong pesto.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers for up to two days. Reheat gently in a skillet with a teaspoon of water, then stir in a small spoonful of fresh pesto after the gnocchi are hot.

name: Quesadilla with Sweet Potato and Black Beans
description: A hearty vegetarian quesadilla filled with mashed sweet potato and beans.
steps: Build: Spread the mashed sweet potato on one half of the tortilla. Top with black beans, cumin, and cheese. Fold over.
Cook: Cook in a dry pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and the cheese is melted. Serve with sour cream and salsa.
notes: You can use leftover baked sweet potato or microwave one for 5 minutes.

name: Zucchini Noodles with Pesto
description: Tender zucchini noodles tossed with basil pesto and parmesan make a light, quick dinner for one.
steps: Saute zucchini: Heat olive oil in a pan. Add garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Add zucchini noodles and toss for 2-3 minutes until just wilted but still crunchy.
Dress: Remove from heat. Toss with pesto. Top with parmesan and any optional additions.
notes: Do not overcook the zucchini. Stop when the strands are just tender so they do not release too much water.
headnote: Zucchini noodles only need a few minutes in the pan. Stop while the strands still have some bite, then take them off the heat before tossing with pesto so the sauce stays bright and the zucchini does not turn watery.
substitutions: No pesto? Toss the zucchini with olive oil, parmesan, lemon, and black pepper instead. Yellow summer squash can replace the zucchini; keep the same short cooking time and stop before the strands soften completely.
storage: Zucchini noodles are best eaten right away because they release water as they sit. If needed, refrigerate leftovers for one day and reheat briefly in a dry pan, then add a fresh spoonful of pesto after warming.

name: Antipasto Skewers
description: All the flavors of an antipasto plate, threaded onto skewers for easy eating.
steps: Thread: Thread the ingredients onto the skewers in any order you like. Arrange on a plate and drizzle with a little of the marinade from the mozzarella.
notes: These are perfect for eating while standing in the kitchen.
headnote: Keep the mozzarella, tomatoes, olives, and cured meat close in size so each skewer has a balanced bite. Drain wet ingredients well before assembly, then finish with olive oil, black pepper, and basil just before serving.
substitutions: Use any combination of small mozzarella balls, firm cheese cubes, olives, cherry tomatoes, marinated artichokes, roasted peppers, or folded salami. Keep the pieces bite-size and choose a mix of creamy, briny, and fresh ingredients.
storage: Assemble these as close to serving as possible. If making them ahead, refrigerate covered for up to one day and add basil, olive oil, and any balsamic finish just before eating so the herbs stay fresh.
